sections.title: Remainders & modular arithmetic
facts: Replace numbers by their remainders before adding, subtracting or multiplying; reduce at the end.
Same remainder $r$ for $p$ and $q$: the number is $r$ more than a multiple of $\text{lcm}(p, q)$.

sections.title: Units digits & cycles
facts: Only the units digits matter: $17^{17}$ ends like $7^{17}$.
Use the exponent mod the cycle length; remainder $0$ is the last digit of the cycle.

sections.title: Number bases
facts: In base $b$ the places are $1, b, b^2, \ldots$ and the digits are $0$ to $b - 1$.
A three-digit number with digits $x, y, z$ in base $b$ is $xb^2 + yb + z$: $213_5 = 2 \cdot 25 + 1 \cdot 5 + 3$.
Into base $b$: divide by $b$ again and again; the remainders read upwards are the digits.

sections.title: Digit problems
facts: A two-digit number is $10a + b$; its reversal is $10b + a$.
Number minus reversal $= 9(a - b)$; number plus reversal $= 11(a + b)$.
$10^n - 1$ is $n$ nines. The first digit is never $0$.

sections.title: Integer equations
facts: $ax + by = c$: find one solution, then step $x$ by $b$ and $y$ by $a$ in opposite directions.
$xy - ax - by = 0$ becomes $(x - b)(y - a) = ab$.
$a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)$: both factors have the same parity.
